summary: Jackson County, OR lookout: 1913 cabin, then a 1916 spar-tree crow's nest; abandoned about 1930; now in ruins per FFLOS and firelookout.com.

facts.design: Crow's nest about 104 feet up in a spar tree, reached by a spiral peg ladder (1916); earlier cabin, and a stone cabin about 1918
facts.status_note: The register and firelookout.com say the site is now in ruins; a 1971 column says the tree had tumbled and the lookout was no more.

events.note: Alidade set on the summit and a cabin built one mile east
Dan Pederson sent to the summit in summer 1915, per a 1971 column
Register: cabin replaced in 1916 by a 104-foot crow's nest on a spiral-ladder tree; firelookout.com says developed in 1915
Lookout phoned the forest supervisor's office in Medford about a new fire near the state line; no crew sent because it lay in another association's territory
Lookout duties transferred to the Old Baldy lookout
Register and firelookout.com say the site was abandoned about 1930; FFLA lists it as Abandoned
Herald and News column (July 1971, quoted by Kemnow) says the fir had tumbled and the lookout was no more

corrections.why: The lookout was a crow's nest on a spar tree with a spiral ladder, per the Show n Tell sheet and Kemnow's page.
The register and firelookout.com both say the site is now in ruins.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says the cabin was replaced in 1916; firelookout.com says the crow's nest was developed in 1915; the Show n Tell sheet gives 1916 through 1930. The story uses 1916 and notes the 1915 date.

Register and Show n Tell give a 104-foot crow's nest; a December 1916 report quoted by Kemnow describes a 99-foot tree topped by an observation box. Both may describe one structure measured differently. facts.height_m uses 104 feet.

Register and firelookout.com say abandoned about 1930. Kemnow says duties moved to Old Baldy in 1924, and his 1971 column gives Pederson 11 years from 1915, which ends about 1926. The story reports both.
Register and firelookout.com say the site is now in ruins; the 1971 column says the fir had tumbled and the lookout was no more. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The 1913-1930 history is well sourced, but Kemnow's page quotes newspapers and the 1971 Herald and News column second-hand; the originals were not read. Nothing read says what stands at the site now or whether it is reachable, so facts.access and visit are omitted. The npshistory cover caption mentions a replica of the lookout tree on Brush Mountain. Its location, date and whether it still stands are unverified, so the story reports only what the caption says. A WebSearch hit for a Pacific Crest Trail loop near Brush Mountain was not used because the link to this peak is unconfirmed. The corrections for kind and status are proposals for the editor. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads.
